morning5_start.name: {name}
morning5_start.text: *Fifth day. It's Sunday, but there's a school event. School uniforms have become more comfortable. Sleeve ends no longer scratch your wrists.*

morning5_mood_high.name: {name}
morning5_mood_high.text: It's the last day. The rooftop key in my pocket touches the back of my hand with every step.

morning5_mood_mid.name: {name}
morning5_mood_mid.text: Last day. Still not sure. But I have to go.

morning5_mood_low.name: {name}
morning5_mood_low.text: The last day. I tap each of the three names left on my lock screen. I can't bring myself to open any of the chat windows.

morning5_seo_note_1.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1.text: *There's a note on my desk. Seoyeon's handwriting. — 'Make some time this afternoon. I'll leave the rooftop unlocked. — Seoyeon'*

morning5_yuna_story_1.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_1.text: *A character in the novel drapes a blanket over someone sleeping in the library. — A scene only I would recognize.*

morning5_return_class.name: {name}
morning5_return_class.text: *Back in the classroom, Dain is waiting.*

morning5_dain_1.name: Dain
morning5_dain_1.text: YO! I signed you up as my partner for today's sports event!

morning5_dain_2.name: Dain
morning5_dain_2.text: Bail on me and I will be SO mad.

morning5_end.name: {name}
morning5_end.text: *I place the notes and notifications from three directions side by side on my desk.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_check.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_check.text: *Event prep time. Walking down the hallway — I pass the empty classroom. The door is open.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_1.text: *The teacher is sitting at the desk. — Not a manuscript this time. She's holding an envelope. A brown envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_2.text: The manuscript. It's unfinished... but I wanted you to see it first.

hidden_homeroom_d5_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_3.text: Haven't shown this to anyone in seven years. — Way outside my job description.

hidden_homeroom_d5_4.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_4.text: ...I take the manuscript. It's heavier than I expected.

hidden_homeroom_d5_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_5.text: ...Showing this to someone else first is more nerve-wracking than I thought.

hidden_homeroom_d5_choice.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_choice.text: *I'm holding the manuscript. The envelope corner presses against my arm.*
choices: I'm sure it came out great. Send it to publishers.
Can I read it for a minute? I'll talk after that.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6.text: ...Then I'll leave it to you. First.

hidden_homeroom_d5_7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_7.text: After you graduate — let's meet. Not as teacher and student.

hidden_homeroom_d5_8.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_8.text: *The teacher turns around. Her long hair sways, and the edge of the clipboard presses against her elbow.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.text: *Last conversation with the homeroom teacher in the empty classroom.*
hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.context: Day 5. Last day. The teacher handed over her 7-year manuscript. A promise to meet after graduation. Tone: Both know this is the last time. Laughing but with a tinge of bittersweetness. More honest than usual, everything feels precious.
hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.personality: The teacher is more honest than usual because it's the last time. Last conversation after handing over the manuscript.

hidden_nurse_d5_check.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_check.text: *Break during the event. Passing by the nurse's office.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1.text: uh? {name}. It's already the last day. Once the event is over, it will really be over.

hidden_nurse_d5_3.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3.text: Can I come by even if I'm not hurt?

hidden_nurse_d5_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_4.text: ...Press it flat so it stays on. — I'm not doing it for you today.

hidden_nurse_d5_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_5.text: ...{name}. Want me to put on a bandage?

hidden_nurse_d5_choice.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice.text: *I'm not hurt. She knows that. She's asking anyway.*
choices: Yes, since it's the last time. Just this once.
Not a bandage — your phone number

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a.text: *She slowly puts the bandage on. There's small writing on it.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a_b.text: ...You said 'just this once.' So why say something like that.

hidden_nurse_d5_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_6.text: I know. I just needed an excuse.

hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.text: *Last conversation with the school nurse outside her office.*
hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.context: Day 5. Last day. The nurse wrote a message on a bandage. A promise to meet after graduation. Tone: Both know this is the last time. Laughing but with a tinge of bittersweetness. More honest than usual, everything feels precious.
hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.personality: The nurse is less playful than usual. Waiting for the day when excuses aren't needed.

morning5_start_b.name: {name}
morning5_start_b.text: *The moment I step into the classroom, attention comes from three directions. A note on my desk, a ribbon tied to a gym uniform string, one notification on my lock screen.*

morning5_start_2_b.name: {name}
morning5_start_2_b.text: *There's a note on my desk. Seoyeon's handwriting.*

morning5_seo_note_1_b.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1_b.text: *I pass by the literature club display in the hallway. My feet stop in front of the bulletin board.*

morning5_seo_note_1_c.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1_c.text: *A short story is posted on the bulletin board. Title: 'To the Person I Met in the Library.' Light purple ink. A small bread crumb clings to the folded corner.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_b.text: *I remember what she said at the cafe yesterday. The manuscript envelope presses heavy against my arm.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_c.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_c.text: *The envelope bends slightly in my hands. Her hand still lingers at the edge of the desk.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_d.text: ...Once you've read it, tell me what you really think. — No need to be polite with me.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_f.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_f.text: You don't have to say that anymore.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_g.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_g.text: *The homeroom teacher pauses for a moment. This time, the attendance sheet does not cover the face.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_h.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_h.text: ...I never thought I'd hear a student say that to me.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_i.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_i.text: *She smooths the folded corner of the manuscript envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_k.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_k.text: *Before answering, I touch the corner of the envelope first.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_m.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_m.text: *Tucking her hair back* ...I don't accept book reports.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_o.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_o.text: *A soft laugh* ...Fine. Write me at least one line.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_p.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_p.text: *The teacher pauses once at the door. She presses the edge of the clipboard twice with her finger, then lets go.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_r.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_r.text: *She stops. Grips her clipboard tight. — Then slowly turns her head.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_s.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_s.text: ...After you graduate. *Her voice cracks.* Yes. After you graduate.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_t.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_t.text: *The teacher swallows the same words again. The edge of the clipboard taps lightly against the doorframe.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_7_b.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_7_b.text: *'Not as teacher and student.' — She's talking about after graduation. Not now, but someday.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_7_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_7_c.text: ...I know. I shouldn't say this now. But today, I'll say this much.

hidden_nurse_d5_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_2_b.text: *The school nurse steps out. She's right in front of me.*

hidden_nurse_d5_4_c.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_4_c.text: *The silence that seemed natural until yesterday is now hanging between paper cups.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_b.text: *After saying it's the last day of the event, the nurse touches her stethoscope once.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1_c.text: *With a light smile* Come visit after graduation.

hidden_nurse_d5_1_f.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_f.text: *'Come by if you're not feeling well.' After saying that, the nurse shifts the hand holding two paper cups slightly.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3_b.text: *The health teacher pauses for a moment. Laughter disappears first.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_e.text: *Smiling again* Ask me that after graduation. — I'll answer then.

hidden_nurse_d5_3_f.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3_f.text: *'After graduating'. It is a closed word, but it remains attached to the back of the hand like the end of a band.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3_g.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_g.text: Go on. You can't skip the event.

hidden_nurse_d5_3_h.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3_h.text: *The school nurse turns to go back inside — and stops.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_b.text: *The health teacher stops laughing. The gaze behind the glasses wavers for a moment.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_d.text: *Adjusting her glasses* ...Fine. But use it after you graduate.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_e.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_e.text: *'After graduating'. The phone number is halfway down the band wrapper.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_f.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_f.text: Want me to put on a bandage?

hidden_nurse_d5_6_b.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_6_b.text: *The nurse takes out a bandage and sticks it on the back of my hand. Slowly. There's tiny writing on the edge of the bandage.*

hidden_nurse_d5_6_c.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_6_c.text: *'After graduation, let's meet at a cafe instead of the nurse's office — ♡' This time, the heart doesn't seem like medical concern.*

morning5_committed_seo.name: {name}
morning5_committed_seo.text: *There's no new note on my desk. Instead, the look in Seoyeon's eyes from the rooftop yesterday is still vivid. Yuna and Dain only say a few short things about getting ready for the event.*

morning5_committed_yuna.name: {name}
morning5_committed_yuna.text: *There isn't any new note. Instead, the way Yuna held my gaze a little too long yesterday is still there. Seoyeon and Dain only say a few short things about getting ready for the event.*

morning5_committed_dain.name: {name}
morning5_committed_dain.text: *Before Dain's exclamation marks, what comes back to me first is the breath that caught at the very end yesterday. Seoyeon and Yuna only say a few short things about getting ready for the event.*

morning5_committed_end.name: {name}
morning5_committed_end.text: *I organize the notes on my desk and check the event schedule for the direction I've already chosen.*

morning5_gate.name: {name}
morning5_gate.text: *The school gate. I stood here five days ago too. My uniform was stiff then — now it fits. It's not just the uniform that changed.*

morning5_yuna_story_2.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_2.text: *The last sentence. 'When that person opened their eyes, I was already gone. I left only a note. — I'll be here again next time.' Light purple ink. The same color as the first note.*

morning5_yuna_story_4.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_4.text: *In the bottom corner of the bulletin board, small text — 'This is fiction. It's not real.' Eraser marks remain.*

morning5_yuna_story_gone.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_gone.text: *Only the pinholes remain on the bulletin board. Where the story should have been. — She took it down. Or maybe she never put it up at all.*

morning5_yuna_story_gone_2.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_gone_2.text: *An empty library seat, a missing bookmark, an unposted novel. Only four thumbtack holes remain on the bulletin board.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_1.text: *The homeroom teacher pauses for a moment. He soon returns to his usual dry expression, but the corners of the envelope are crumpled.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_3.text: I mean — it's bound to be good. You spent seven years on it.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_5.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_5.text: *The teacher reaches out. Takes the manuscript back. Slowly. Slides it back into the envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_6.text: Forget it. Sorry for taking your time.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_8.text: I sent it to publishers three times in seven years. All rejected. Two of those three rejection letters started with — 'Seven years is impressive. I'm sure it's wonderful.'

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_9.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_9.text: *The phrase rejection is stuck in my eyes. It's exactly like what I just said.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_10.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_10.text: ...I thought you'd actually read it and tell me. — I showed it to you because I figured a student wouldn't feel obligated to be kind.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_11.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_11.text: Go on. You'll be late for the event.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_12.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_12.text: *I left and closed the classroom door. The envelope is still on the teacher's desk. A return-label mark the size of a fingernail remains on the surface.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_1.text: *The homeroom teacher stops. The hand holding the clipboard takes strength. The end of the paper is slightly curved.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_3.text: Yes. I don't want to just say something.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_4.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_4.text: All right. — Give me a second.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_5.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_5.text: *When I open the envelope, the smell of paper rises. The end of the last page is blank. Beneath a sentence crossed out in red, traces of starting again and stopping overlap.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_7.text: My hand stops whenever I look at the last page. It has for years.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_8.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_8.text: *The teacher swallows the rest. The classroom goes quiet, as quiet as the empty last line.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_9.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_9.text: Let's look at that line together.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_11.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_11.text: Yes. I'm reading it right now.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_12.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_12.text: *Homeroom teacher laughs. The corners of the eyes relax before the corners of the mouth, and the clipboard goes down on the desk.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_14.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_14.text: *She cradles the manuscript again. The teacher rubs the return-label mark with her thumb. The paper edge crumples slightly in her palm.*
